hej.nota: You can use it at any time of day and with anyone.

farvel.nota: The r is not pronounced: it blends into the a.
farvel.consejo: The r is barely heard: «fah-vel», stress on «vel».

vi ses.consejo: Read it as it looks, with a clear s at the end.

tak.consejo: The vowel is like the «a» in «father», and the final «k» is short and clear.

mange tak.nota: The «ng» sounds like in «sing», but without pronouncing the g at all.
mange tak.consejo: The «ng» is like in «sing», without pronouncing a g.

ja.nota: The usual pronunciation has an «a» sound; there is also a more open variant, close to the English «yeah».
ja.consejo: The Danish j sounds like the «y» in «yes».

nej.consejo: Like «nigh» in English: the final j turns into an «ee» sound.

hvordan.nota: «hv» is simply read as «v». The r is not pronounced.
hvordan.consejo: «hv» is read as «v»; the r and the final d are barely heard.

har.nota: It's the same for every person: jeg har, du har…
har.consejo: The final r is not pronounced.

trad.en: you have / I have (the verb «to have»)

det.nota: It isn't translated here: it is part of the expression «have det godt» (to be well, to feel good).
det.consejo: The final t is not pronounced: «deh».

jeg.nota: It's spelled with a g, but it sounds like «yie».
jeg.consejo: It's spelled with a g, but it sounds like «yie».

godt.nota: The final «t» is not pronounced separately; the «d» is very soft and can sound voiceless.
godt.consejo: Roughly «got», with a very soft «d» at the end.

hvad.nota: The h is silent and the final d almost disappears.
hvad.consejo: The h and the d are not pronounced: just «vah».

med.nota: The final d sounds very soft or disappears.
med.consejo: The final d is very soft or disappears.

dig.nota: It's spelled with a g, but it sounds like «dye».
dig.consejo: It's spelled with a g, but it sounds like «dye».

også.nota: Neither the g nor the å sounds the way you'd expect.
også.consejo: It sounds like «AW-suh»: neither the g nor the å sounds the way you'd expect.

hvor.nota: The o is open and a little long, like «aw» in «saw». The r is not pronounced.
hvor.consejo: «hv» = v; the final r is not pronounced.

hedder.nota: The d is soft, like the «th» in «this». The final -er sounds like a short «uh».
hedder.consejo: The dd sounds like the «th» in «this»; the final -er sounds like a short «uh».

trad.en: is called / my name is / your name is (the verb «at hedde», to be called)
is / am / are (the verb «at være», to be)

kommer.nota: The final -er sounds like a short «uh».
kommer.consejo: The final -er sounds like a short «uh».

trad.en: you come / I come (the verb «at komme», to come)

fra.nota: The Danish r is pronounced in the throat, a bit like the French r. It doesn't vibrate like a rolled r.
fra.consejo: The Danish r is made in the throat, like a soft gargled «h».

bor.consejo: The final r turns into a soft «uh» sound.

trad.en: you live / I live (the verb «at bo», to live)

danmark.consejo: There is no «r» in this word: say «dan-mahk», with a short, quiet «k» at the end.

københavn.nota: There is no ö sound in English: round your lips as if to say «oh», then say «eh».

taler.consejo: The a sounds like «ah», and the final -er like a short «uh».

trad.en: you speak / I speak (the verb «at tale», to speak)

lidt.nota: The final «d» is very weak and may sound voiceless.
lidt.consejo: Roughly «lit», with a very weak «d» at the end.

dansk.nota: Languages are written in lowercase in Danish, unlike in English, where they start with a capital letter.

nul.consejo: The u sounds like the «oo» in «food», but a little shorter.

en.nota: It is also an article: «en kop» = «a cup».

tre.nota: Remember: the Danish r is pronounced in the throat.

fire.consejo: The final -re sounds like a short «uh».

otte.nota: The double t sounds soft, almost like a d.

ni.consejo: Like the English «knee», without the k.

kan.consejo: The a sounds like the «a» in «father».

te.consejo: Like the «ay» in «day», with a clear «t» in front.

glas.consejo: Like English «glass», but with an «ah» sound.

tyve.consejo: y = say «ee» with your lips rounded as for «oo».

tømrer.consejo: ö = say «eh» with your lips rounded as for «oh».

sprog.consejo: The final g is close to a semi-vowel like «oo».

mobilnummer.consejo: In «nummer», the unstressed -er ending is reduced; it isn't a general rule for all words.

mail.consejo: It's the same as in English.

kursus.consejo: The r changes the vowel before it; it isn't pronounced as a separate English r.

næste.consejo: æ = an open «e», like the «e» in «bed».

tretten.consejo: The «e» is like the «e» in «bed»; the «tt» is pronounced as a soft d.

fjorten.consejo: «Fj» sounds close to «fy»; the r changes the vowel, and the ending sounds roughly like «den».

femten.consejo: The «e» is open, like the «e» in «bed»; in «-ten», the t softens to a d sound.
